name: Slant
rules: Draw a diagonal in every cell. A number says how many diagonals touch that corner; corners with no number are free. The diagonals must never join up into a loop.
technique.1: This number already has all the lines it needs, so every other cell around it must slant away from it.
technique.2: This number still needs exactly as many lines as it has empty cells around it, so all of those cells must slant towards it.
technique.3: The two corners this line would join are already linked by a chain of lines, so joining them would close a loop, and the cell must slant the other way.
technique.4: This line would join two groups of lines that never reach the edge of the grid and have no other way out, sealing them into a loop, so the cell must slant the other way.
technique.5: The numbers between this cell and the highlighted filled cell can only be met if the two slant the same way, so copy the filled cell.
technique.6: Two neighbouring empty cells around this number must slant the same way, so between them they give it exactly one line, and that settles the other cells around it.
demo.1: Every cell gets one diagonal. It can lean either way, but no cell is left empty.
demo.2: A number counts the diagonals that touch that corner. Two touch this 2, so it is done.
demo.3: The same diagonal ends on a corner with no number. Those corners count nothing, so they never limit you.
demo.4: This corner needs four, so all four cells around it have to point at it. There is only one way to do that.
demo.5: These four have joined up into a closed ring. Rings are not allowed, so one of them must lean the other way.
demo.6: Every cell filled, every number matched, and no ring anywhere.
